schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: The first cocoon stage as a device: raw design prose (a conversation excerpt, a note, a held-* record) in, a CANDIDATE intention out — {what, why, anchors, read}, exactly four fields. The DRAFT comes through the caller-injected resolve seam (inference_domain.resolve — the sole path to the host; metered, cached, so the same source is a genuine cache HIT on re-extraction). The JUDGMENT is deterministic: CHECKS (cairn/devices/intention_extractor/extractor.py) refuse a draft whose anchors are not verbatim in the source (anchors_verbatim) or whose field-set drifts / whose why is silent (record_shape); a refusal carries every finding first-pass. `extract()` is one crossing and breadcrumbs its verdict — PASS, REFUSED, and UNPARSEABLE alike. Live wiring: `python3 -m cairn.devices.intention_extractor.live <file> [model]` (live.py — the first composition of domain.resolve + host.ollama_resolver outside inference_domain's own proofs). THE CHECKS ARE HELD, NOT HOUSED: they berth as this device's own machine at machines/judge/ and are re-exported here as the published surface. The device drafts and dials; the judge grades and reaches nothing.
why: Akien, 2026-07-24, verbatim: 'the librarian will have you build something, and you and i can move, say, intention extraction to an agent. then when you get the build ticket, you do the build... and then go back and run the inspection over the initial intention extraction... until initial intention extraction is a settled issue.' CC is the most expensive resolver; moving extraction to a watchable, optimizable stage spends it parsimoniously (Law 1 applied to the pipeline itself). Ordering is his too, 2026-07-27: 'i was going to try and do the intention extractor as a device first, but i see that now we start with CC and work outwards' — built AFTER CC's tooling ring, so the extractor arrives to find its judge already seated: a draft is graded by deterministic checks (and its component by the build gate), never by CC's opinion, the least independent witness. The founding defect it exists to end: FABRICATED ATTRIBUTION — 2026-07-26, 'the graph type is a coordinate, not a class' recorded as Akien's ruling when it was CC's inference; only seven words of the embedding claim were his. The anchor discipline makes that structurally impossible to smuggle: what the source does not literally say lives under `read`, labeled.
invoke: import: `from cairn.devices.intention_extractor.extractor import IntentionExtractorDevice`. Prove: `python3 cairn/devices/intention_extractor/proofs/test_intention_extractor.py` (exit 0 = green; no host, no DB). Live: `python3 -m cairn.devices.intention_extractor.live <source-file> [model]` (defaults qwen2.5:7b; exit 0 PASS / 1 REFUSED).
for_whom: WHO OPERATES ON THE FINDINGS — sorted 2026-08-06 at Akien's instruction, on his definition (findings are the result of an inspector, for something else to operate on). The answer was already settled and already written, in extractor.py's own header: 'A refused draft is a VERDICT, not an anomaly — returned with its findings for the caller (CC today, the librarian later) to dispose.' It is lifted here because the INTENTION is the living spec — the most authoritative artifact outside Akien's head (his ruling, 2026-08-06) — and a consumer recorded only in a docstring is the design living somewhere the design is not read. So: CC TODAY disposes a refusal (fix the anchor, re-run the source, or kill the draft); THE LIBRARIAN LATER takes that seat, which is the whole point of the cocoon — the stage exists to keep the expensive resolver off the settled, and a refusal a human has to read is that saving only half-made. MEASURED STATE, not the aspiration: live.py is the ONLY non-proof caller of extract(), and it prints the findings to a terminal and exits 1. There is no automatic retry, so today's dispose is literally a person reading text. That is a real gap in the cocoon and is named as one rather than papered over.
entry: FRESH build. The check-registry-with-required-provenance shape is deliberate reuse of orient's scans / build_inspector's filters (the learning-device pattern, third instance — the pattern is now load-bearing across the tooling ring); the anchor discipline is Cairn's own, seeded by the 2026-07-26 attribution failure. Nothing carried from the quarry.
state_and_history: compiled to state.json (projected window) + history.json (append-only voyage) beside this charter — the charter-state-history split.
how_it_learns: Two loops, one per judge. (1) THE CHECKS learn from caught failures: when Akien (or a downstream build) catches a bad extraction a deterministic check could have caught, that check joins CHECKS carrying the failure as Provenance in its docstring — the proof refuses a check with no dated correction, and pins the registry so joining means joining the teeth (learns-its-gates, third instrument). Founding set: anchors_verbatim ← the 2026-07-26 fabricated attribution; record_shape ← the charter filename forcing the why + the VALIDATION exactly-eight rule. (2) THE GROUND TRUTH is downstream and measured, not opined: an extraction was GOOD if the build it fed proved out, BAD if it kicked back (Akien's cocoon design, with CC a temporary stand-in until proof-history can replace it). That loop's meter does not exist yet — filed edge (b) — and until it does, 'settled enough to rely on' (Akien's bar: ~2-3 clean tickets) is unmeasurable, deliberately not faked.
filed_edges: (a) THE COCOON LOOP IS NOT CLOSED: today CC calls extract() by hand; the designed flow (librarian drives → extractor drafts → CC builds → CC free-rides the pass to inspect the extraction and grow the checks) waits on the librarian. The device is the stage, not the pipeline.

(b) THE PROOF-OUTCOME METER: 'an extraction was good if the build it fed proved out' needs the link extraction→ticket→verdict recorded somewhere queryable before 'settled' (Akien's 2-3-clean-tickets bar) is a measurement rather than taste. Unbuilt; the falsifier below names the wrong-shape signal meanwhile.

(c) SEMANTIC anchor checking: anchors_verbatim catches invented QUOTES, not kept-words-with-swapped-MEANINGS (words-kept-meanings-replaced — the drift that hides). A deterministic check for that does not exist yet and pretending one does would be a hollow gate; today that catch is CC's and Akien's, by read.

(d) BERTH DISPOSITION: the extractor returns a candidate; WHERE it berths (code-seam charter vs commons intention vs ticket) is the caller's call today. The which-root decision tree (CLAUDE.md 'Which root?') is prose a later check or the librarian could carry.

(e) draft RETRY on UNPARSEABLE (one re-ask with the parse error quoted) — deliberately not built: a retry loop is where token spend hides; the loud refusal is the honest v0. Revisit when live UNPARSEABLE rates are measured, not guessed.
gates: proof gate — proofs/test_intention_extractor.py (11 teeth) under the tester. Durability gate: committed + pushed. Build gate: journaled PROVEME exit inspected (this component was born under the wired gate — the first component whose whole voyage ran with the judge seated).
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) a draft with a fabricated anchor PASSES (tooth 2 — the founding defect readmitted); (2) a candidate is returned REPAIRED rather than judged (tooth 1 asserts unchanged — a stage that silently fixes drafts is training its own blind spot); (3) an empty source or absent seam produces a candidate (teeth 6-7 — invention from nothing); (4) a check joins CHECKS without a dated correction (tooth 8); (5) extractor.py grows an outbound-capable import (tooth 11 — a second door to the host); (6) a REFUSED or UNPARSEABLE crossing leaves no breadcrumb (teeth 4, 9 — a silent refusal is the silent-device defect reborn). WRONG-SHAPE SIGNAL: if the checks registry is static three caught-bad-extractions from now, the learning half is hollow; and if extractions are never fed to real builds, the ground-truth loop (edge b) never closes and this device is a prompt wrapper wearing a charter; (7) THE CHECKS COMING BACK INTO THIS COMPONENT. They berth as machines/judge/ because bin/cmd/determinism read this component as a GATE that could reach an oracle at SLEEP (live.py) — true since the device was built, and invisible until the checks imported the gate tool on 2026-08-13. A check defined here again, or this module importing cairn.tools.gate directly, is the carve-out undone; (8) an extraction breadcrumb naming only ``checks_failed`` — a PASS must say which lanes RAN, or a lane that stops running writes the same triumphant crumb; (9) a second whitespace ruler appearing here beside the judge's ``normalized`` — the anchor compare and the source floor measure with one.
proof: proofs/test_intention_extractor.py — grounded draft passes unchanged; fabricated anchor refused with the quote carried whole; empty why and field drift named both ways; unparseable draft loud with raw draft whole, still breadcrumbed; fenced draft parses; empty source never touches the host; no seam no extraction; every check taught and pinned; crossings breadcrumb PASS/REFUSED alike, reads silent; device-hood + Form v0 #2; import-purity by AST. Green: `python3 cairn/devices/intention_extractor/proofs/test_intention_extractor.py`.
owner: CC owns the code + proofs and gates writes to them. Akien owns the design (the cocoon, the stage ordering, the settled-bar) and the disposition of candidates into the intention layer (the control surface is his).
provenance: Born 2026-07-27, immediately after the six silent devices were disposed and the whole-repo sweep read zero — the moment CC's tooling ring closed. First device born under the wired build gate and born instrumented (the silent-devices lesson applied at birth, not retrofitted). Its first live extraction (live.py, qwen2.5:7b through inference_domain) was run on the very 2026-07-24 conversation excerpt that founded it. Naming settled by ruling 2026-08-09-the-intentions-model-checker-is-one-llm-call (correcting a typo'd 'inference' in the 2026-08-08 packet): this device keeps its name; the 'intentions model checker' — the intentions-SEARCHING device, one LLM call over the compiled model, unbuilt, casts its own ticket when work starts — is a sibling, not this.
learns: Yes; it learns from verdicts on intent extraction accuracy.
